speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: asked the Prime Minister in light of the Auditor-General's observations with regard to IT lapses in the Report of the Auditor-General for FY 2018/2019 and similar observations in preceding years (a) what are the systemic reasons that explain these repetitive findings; and (b) what are the findings of the major audit on public sector IT systems carried out from 2009-2011.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Some agencies also had lapses in the conduct of regular reviews of security controls in their systems, including the validity of access rights.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: GovTech has tightened the rules and guidelines to improve governance processes by agencies in these areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Such manual processes can result in delays and errors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The use of automated solutions will facilitate compliance but will still require supervision and oversight by our officers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Officers must also be alert to situations where IT lapses can occur and flag these up.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Thus, we will also continue to raise IT security awareness and capabilities among our public officers.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: My question pertains to the second part of the original Parliamentary Question – the three-year-long IT processes audit that was carried out in the public sector.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: What was it prompted by, such an extensive review?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Were these issues brought up and was there a review of the Government Instruction Manual, for example, to ensure that access rights ought to be more heavily controlled?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The 2018 to 2019 findings were largely whether individuals were able to easily comply with the manual implementation of processes and policies that were already in place.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, the two audits in 2009 and then subsequently 10 years later, both covered vendor management and access rights, but from very different perspectives.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: In the latter case, it was largely about the individuals' ability to comply with sometimes very onerous or very complex policies.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: In the first instance, 10 years ago, it was largely about whether the agencies had processes in place and whether they were reviewing those processes adequately.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: As for the first question, I do not know if there was one specific factor that I can point to.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But I would be happy to get back to the Member about what triggered the audit.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: My assumption would be that this was part of the ongoing review that public agencies would take for risk mitigation, where areas of concern are audited.
